significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) law that per-item “required depth” and the “Truncation Gap” increase with typological/script distance and low resource level, predict cross-lingual errors, and causally distinguish unfinished computation from absent knowledge; it also includes the form-(ii) claim that “granting extra late-layer compute ... recovers correct answers specifically on high-required-depth items.” This establishes both a broad behavioral regularity and a causal mechanism, fixing expectations for depth trajectories, error attribution, and compute interventions across languages rather than merely identifying a decodable direction; work on adaptive depth such as Schuster et al.’s Confident Adaptive Language Modeling illustrates that such compute-allocation conclusions can affect model inference decisions. Refutation would still be informative by ruling out fixed-depth truncation as a major explanation for multilingual gaps, and true and false outcomes are sharply distinguishable; after topic substitution, generic questions about language-independent versus language-specific mechanisms would not retain this law or causal decomposition, so the score is supported by claim-specific content rather than the topic alone.

reach.justification: The transferable handles are the per-item “required depth,” the “Truncation Gap,” and “adaptive per-item depth allocation” that can route “only high-required-depth items to extra compute”; this is an ex-ante deployment handle because it can flag a still-unfinished run and allocate more computation before its answer is accepted. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive prediction survives as a relation—greater distance or lower resources should imply deeper required computation, larger truncation gaps, and concentrated recovery—rather than merely supplying a procedure that must rediscover an unconstrained direction, although the specific late-layer-looping intervention may remain architecture-sensitive. The hypothesis is stated across multilingual model families, tasks, and languages, with deployment teams as downstream users; substituting the bare multilingual-representation topic removes the routing metric, scaling relation, and action window, so the reach is particular to this claim rather than inherited from the topic.
